User: Write a memoir in first person about your experience as a single mom, including the challenges and triumphs you faced, how you balanced work and family life, and any lessons or advice you would give to other single mothers. Use descriptive language to paint a vivid picture of your journey, and be honest and vulnerable about your emotions and experiences. Consider including anecdotes, dialogue, and reflections on your growth and personal development throughout your time as a single parent.
Assistant: When I became a single mom, my entire life turned upside down. Suddenly, I had to not only provide for myself but also for my child. It was a challenging and emotional journey full of highs and lows, but I learned so much along the way.

Balancing work and family life was never easy as a single mom. I had to juggle motherhood, a full-time job, and other responsibilities all at once. Sometimes, it felt like there weren't enough hours in the day. But, I was determined to make it work. I learned to prioritize and manage my time wisely. I had to make sacrifices and adjust to the ever-changing needs of my child, but I never lost sight of my ultimate goal. 

One of my biggest challenges as a single mom was financial struggles. Being the sole provider and breadwinner meant that money was always tight. There were times when I had to choose between buying groceries or paying bills. But, I never gave up. I worked hard and made every penny count. I learned to be resourceful and creative, finding ways to save money and make ends meet. 

There were many triumphs along the way. Every time my child achieved something, like learning to read or graduating from school, it felt like a victory for both of us. Watching my child grow and thrive was the best feeling in the world. Knowing that I was able to provide for my child and give them a happy childhood made all the struggles worth it. 

My journey as a single mom taught me many valuable lessons. I learned the importance of self-care and asking for help when needed. I became more independent and resilient. I learned to be patient and flexible, adapting to unexpected changes and challenges. My experiences made me a stronger and more compassionate person.

To other single moms out there, my advice would be to never give up. It's okay to ask for help, and it's okay to make mistakes. You are not alone, and there is nothing wrong with being a single parent. Your love and dedication for your child are what truly matter. Cherish the small moments and take things one day at a time. Remember, you are capable of amazing things. 

Overall, my journey as a single mom was a roller coaster ride filled with tears, laughter, and love. It was challenging, but also incredibly rewarding. I am grateful for the experience, and I know that it made me a better person and mother.
User: Can you add some anecdotes about specific challenges you faced as a single mom?
Assistant: Absolutely! One specific challenge I faced as a single mom was finding affordable and reliable childcare. I remember working a double shift at my job one day and coming home to find out that the person I had hired to watch my child had cancelled last minute. I had to call in sick the following day because I didn't have anyone else to watch my child. It was tough because I needed that income to support us, but I also couldn't leave my child alone. Another challenge was trying to balance my career aspirations with my parenting responsibilities. I remember feeling torn between taking on professional opportunities and spending time with my child. One time, I was offered a promotion at work that would require me to work long hours and travel frequently. After a lot of reflection, I ultimately declined the offer because I didn't want to sacrifice precious moments with my child. It was a difficult decision, but I knew it was the right one for us. During holidays and birthdays, I also struggled with wanting to give my child the world, but having to stick to a tight budget. I remember one year, my child really wanted a gaming console that was way out of my price range. I worked extra shifts and saved up for months to surprise them with the console on their birthday. Seeing their face light up when they saw it was the best feeling in the world. These challenges taught me to be resourceful, flexible, and persistent. I learned to always have a backup plan and to never give up.
User: Given the text: What is a family? Each of the first 3 stanzas uses a different simile to explain how deep and lasting the connection between family members is. Similies are figures of speech that expresses a resemblance between things of different kinds, using the word like or as. A family is like the stars. Who support and always care. A family is like a book. Their love is always near. A family is many things. And how they teach you so you know. Or if through time it's been so worn. They're split up and always torn. Your family will always be. And will be a part of you eternally. This poem really touched me. There was a family when my grandparents lived. There is a family of my own now (my son and my daughter). I very much wish that they have their own families and think about us. I relate to everything when I read this poem. My family is going through a tough time - relationship problems. I want them to read this poem to get the real meaning of a family and their duties as a family. I love my sister and brother-in-law, but at this point I dislike both of them and what they're doing to the children and themselves. God will make a miracle way for them. Family is what we need to keep us safe if someone gets hurt our family is always there no matter what it is. We should care and love our family. We should cooperate one another do household chores, make fun, and enjoy and relax. But remember sleep is the most priority thing we should do. I am the secretary for our church and was searching a poem to put in our bulletin as we celebrate "Family Month" in October. We celebrate our church anniversary in October as well and this year we celebrate our 120th Anniversary. We know that it is power of families that has kept our church continuing to grow...a church of many generations. Can you suggest a way for me to convey the message of this poem to my family who are going through tough times in their relationships?
Assistant: One way to convey the message of this poem to your family is to share it with them and take time to discuss its meaning and relevance to your family's situation. Encourage everyone to listen to each other's thoughts and feelings, and emphasize the importance of supporting and caring for one another as a family. Remind them that no matter what challenges they may face, their family will always be there for them and that they are all connected by a deep and lasting bond. Finally, encourage them to work together to overcome their difficulties and to strengthen their family relationships.
User: I think I will print out this poem for my family and read it together with them. Is there any advice you can give on how to start the discussion? What are some questions that I can ask to encourage everyone to share their thoughts and feelings?

1. What does the phrase "a family is like the stars" mean to you? 2. Can you think of any examples where our family has shown "support and caring" like the stars in the sky? 3. What are some of the ways that families show their love and support for one another, according to the lines "a family is like a book, their love is always near"? 4. Why do you think the poem says that a family will always be a part of you eternally? 5. How can we apply the message of this poem to our current situation as a family? Encourage everyone to share their thoughts and feelings openly and without judgment. Emphasize that this is a safe space for everyone to express themselves, and that the goal is to support each other and strengthen our family connection. Best of luck!

Can you explain how Family Learning Programmes provide parents and carers an opportunity to step back into learning?
Assistant: Family Learning Programmes provide parents and carers an opportunity to step back into learning by offering courses that aim to equip them with the necessary skills to support their children's learning. These courses are designed to be delivered in a relaxed and friendly environment, where parents and carers can learn and develop new skills without feeling overwhelmed. The programmes are run in partnership with schools and community groups and are usually held in local schools or community settings. By providing this opportunity for parents and carers to learn alongside their children, Family Learning Programmes help to build their confidence, enable them to develop new skills and create a positive learning environment for the whole family. This not only benefits the children who receive additional support at home but also empowers parents and carers to take an active role in their family's education.
User: Can you suggest some specific courses that are typically offered in Family Learning Programmes to help parents and carers support their child's learning?
Assistant: Surely! The specific courses offered in Family Learning Programmes may vary depending on the needs of the community or school. However, some examples of courses that are typically offered include:

1. Literacy and Numeracy: These courses aim to develop parents' and carers' foundational literacy and numeracy skills so that they can better support their child's learning.

2. Technology and Digital Skills: These courses aim to teach parents and carers how to use computers, the internet, and other digital devices to help support their child's learning.

3. English for Speakers of Other Languages (ESOL): These courses aim to provide language support for parents and carers who do not speak English as their first language, enabling them to better support their child's learning.

4. Parenting Skills: These courses provide parents and carers with skills and strategies to help them improve their parenting abilities and support their children's emotional wellbeing.

5. Health and Wellbeing: These courses aim to provide parents and carers with information on healthy living, mental health, and wellbeing, enabling them to promote a healthy lifestyle for their children.

These are just a few examples of the courses that may be offered in Family Learning Programmes.
User: Can you provide information on how parents and carers can enroll in Family Learning Programmes?
Assistant: Absolutely! Enrolling in Family Learning Programmes varies depending on the specific programme that a school or community organisation offers, but here are some general steps that parents and carers can follow:

1. Check with your child's school or with a local community organisation to see if they offer Family Learning Programmes.

2. Attend an information session or parents' meeting to learn about the specific courses that are being offered.

3. Sign up for the course or courses that are of interest to you. In some cases, you may need to fill out an enrolment form or provide basic information about yourself.

4. Make arrangements for childcare if needed. Some family learning programmes offer on-site childcare, while others may refer parents to local childcare providers.

5. Attend the classes and actively participate in the learning experience. This may involve completing assignments, attending workshops, and engaging with other parents and carers.

By enrolling in Family Learning Programmes, parents and carers can gain valuable skills for supporting their child's learning while also having the opportunity to engage in lifelong learning in a supportive and welcoming environment.

4. In Australia, the Early Learning, Every Day Every Way (ELEDEW) project has been developed to provide families with the skills to better support their child's learning and development. The programme includes courses on literacy, numeracy, and digital skills, as well as parenting skills.

These are just a few examples of schools and community groups that have successfully implemented Family Learning Programmes around the world.

3. Prepare the soil: Make sure that your soil is rich in nutrients and has good drainage. You may need to add some compost or other organic matter to the soil to improve its fertility.

User: I think I'll try growing marigolds and zinnias in my garden. Do you have any tips on how to make the flowers last longer once I cut them?

1. Cut the flowers in the morning: This is when the flowers are most hydrated, which can help them last longer in a vase.

2. Use clean water and a clean vase: Make sure the vase is clean and free of bacteria. Use room temperature water, as cold water can shock the flowers.

3. Cut the stems at an angle: Cut the stems at a 45-degree angle, which creates a larger surface area for the flowers to absorb water.

4. Remove any leaves below the waterline: This helps prevent bacteria growth and keeps the water clean.

5. Change the water every 2-3 days: Fresh water can help keep the flowers hydrated and extend their vase life.

User: Given the text: Family Learning Programmes are run in partnership with schools and community groups. These courses aim to provide parents and carers with the skills they need to support children through school years.
They also give parents and carers an opportunity to take a step back into learning in a relaxed and friendly environment.
Courses are usually run on an outreach basis in local schools or community settings.
Can you explain how Family Learning Programmes provide parents and carers an opportunity to step back into learning?
Assistant: Family Learning Programmes provide parents and carers an opportunity to step back into learning by offering courses that aim to equip them with the necessary skills to support their children's learning. These courses are designed to be delivered in a relaxed and friendly environment, where parents and carers can learn and develop new skills without feeling overwhelmed. The programmes are run in partnership with schools and community groups and are usually held in local schools or community settings. By providing this opportunity for parents and carers to learn alongside their children, Family Learning Programmes help to build their confidence, enable them to develop new skills and create a positive learning environment for the whole family. This not only benefits the children who receive additional support at home but also empowers parents and carers to take an active role in their family's education.
User: Can you suggest some specific courses that are typically offered in Family Learning Programmes to help parents and carers support their child's learning?
Assistant: Surely! The specific courses offered in Family Learning Programmes may vary depending on the needs of the community or school. However, some examples of courses that are typically offered include:

1. Literacy and Numeracy: These courses aim to develop parents' and carers' foundational literacy and numeracy skills so that they can better support their child's learning.

2. Technology and Digital Skills: These courses aim to teach parents and carers how to use computers, the internet, and other digital devices to help support their child's learning.

3. English for Speakers of Other Languages (ESOL): These courses aim to provide language support for parents and carers who do not speak English as their first language, enabling them to better support their child's learning.

4. Parenting Skills: These courses provide parents and carers with skills and strategies to help them improve their parenting abilities and support their children's emotional wellbeing.

5. Health and Wellbeing: These courses aim to provide parents and carers with information on healthy living, mental health, and wellbeing, enabling them to promote a healthy lifestyle for their children.

These are just a few examples of the courses that may be offered in Family Learning Programmes.
User: Can you provide information on how parents and carers can enroll in Family Learning Programmes?
Assistant: Absolutely! Enrolling in Family Learning Programmes varies depending on the specific programme that a school or community organisation offers, but here are some general steps that parents and carers can follow:

1. Check with your child's school or with a local community organisation to see if they offer Family Learning Programmes.

2. Attend an information session or parents' meeting to learn about the specific courses that are being offered.

3. Sign up for the course or courses that are of interest to you. In some cases, you may need to fill out an enrolment form or provide basic information about yourself.

4. Make arrangements for childcare if needed. Some family learning programmes offer on-site childcare, while others may refer parents to local childcare providers.

5. Attend the classes and actively participate in the learning experience. This may involve completing assignments, attending workshops, and engaging with other parents and carers.

By enrolling in Family Learning Programmes, parents and carers can gain valuable skills for supporting their child's learning while also having the opportunity to engage in lifelong learning in a supportive and welcoming environment.

These are just a few examples of schools and community groups that have successfully implemented Family Learning Programmes around the world.

User: Please compile a comprehensive and practical list of tips that individuals working from home can follow to maintain focus and minimize distractions. The list should cover a range of aspects, including but not limited to setting up a dedicated workspace, establishing clear boundaries with family members or housemates, implementing effective time-management strategies, minimizing digital distractions, staying physically and mentally active during breaks, and utilizing tools and technologies that aid productivity. It should also consider the unique challenges that remote work can pose and offer solutions that are achievable and sustainable. Finally, the tips should be presented in a clear and organized format, with actionable steps that readers can apply immediately.
Assistant: 1. Set up a dedicated workspace
- Choose a quiet and comfortable space where you can work without interruptions
- Keep your workspace organized and clutter-free
- Invest in a comfortable chair and desk to support good posture

2. Establish clear boundaries
- Communicate your work hours with family members or housemates
- Ask them to respect your work time and avoid unnecessary interruptions
- Use a "Do Not Disturb" sign or noise-cancelling headphones to signal when you're working

3. Implement effective time management strategies
- Make a to-do list or schedule for each day and stick to it
- Prioritize urgent tasks and tackle them early in the morning
- Use a timer or Pomodoro technique to work in focused bursts with regular breaks

4. Minimize digital distractions
- Turn off notifications on your phone or computer during work hours
- Use browser extensions to block social media or other distracting websites
- Avoid multitasking and focus on one task at a time

5. Stay physically and mentally active during breaks
- Take short breaks to stretch, go for a walk, or do some light exercise
- Practice mindfulness or meditation to reduce stress and improve mental clarity
- Socialize with family members or housemates to recharge your energy

6. Utilize tools and technologies to aid productivity
- Use project management tools to track progress and collaborate with team members
- Download productivity apps such as Trello or Evernote to stay organized and focused
- Use a noise-cancelling microphone or headset for clearer communication during virtual meetings

7. Address unique challenges of remote work
- Create a routine and stick to it to maintain a sense of structure and normalcy
- Take breaks from screens by reading a book or engaging in a non-work-related hobby
- Take care of your mental health by seeking support from colleagues, family, or mental health professionals when needed

In conclusion, working from home requires discipline, boundaries, and clear strategies to be productive and focused. By setting up a dedicated workspace, establishing clear boundaries with family members or housemates, implementing effective time-management strategies, minimizing digital distractions, staying physically and mentally active during breaks, utilizing tools and technologies that aid productivity, and addressing unique challenges of remote work, you can create a conducive environment for work and achieve your goals efficiently.
User: Can you please suggest some more apps or tools that can help me with productivity and time management? Also, do you have any advice on how to stay motivated while working alone at home?
Assistant: Sure, here are some apps and tools that may help with productivity and time management:

1. RescueTime - A time tracking app that gives you detailed reports on how much time you spend on different activities on your computer and mobile devices. 2. Focus@Will - A music streaming service designed to improve focus and productivity by delivering scientifically selected music according to your preferences. 3. Trello - A collaborative and intuitive project management tool that visualizes tasks and progress through boards and cards. 4. Forest - A gamified app that helps you focus by planting virtual trees that grow as long as you stay away from your phone. 5. Todoist - A simple yet powerful task manager that lets you create to-do lists, set priority levels, and receive reminders. As for staying motivated while working alone at home, here are some tips:

1. Create a daily routine and stick to it. A consistent routine helps you establish a sense of normalcy and keeps you on track. 2. Set realistic goals and break them down into smaller, achievable tasks. Celebrate each milestone you reach to stay motivated. 3. Take regular breaks and switch up your routine with different activities to avoid burnout and increase creativity. 4. Connect with colleagues or friends through virtual channels to share progress, updates, and support each other. 5. Reward yourself for completing tasks or meeting deadlines with something that you enjoy, such as a favorite snack or a short walk outside. Remember, staying motivated also requires self-awareness and kindness towards yourself. Don't be too hard on yourself if things don't go as planned, and give yourself credit for the effort you put in.

User: Hi, I'm looking for some new music to listen to. Can you recommend anything?
Assistant: I'd be happy to help. What kind of music are you into? Do you have a preferred genre or artist?
User: I like a mix of everything, but I've been listening to a lot of folk and ambient music lately.
Assistant: Great taste! There are some amazing artists in those genres. Have you heard of Tim Hecker or William Basinski?
User: Yeah, I've listened to them before. But I'm looking for something a bit more obscure. Maybe something that's been overlooked or underappreciated.
Assistant: Okay, I think I can help you with that. There are a lot of hidden gems out there. Can you give me a hint about what you're looking for? For example, do you want something more experimental or something more mellow?
User: Hmm, I think I'd like something that's a bit of both. Something that's experimental but also has a soothing quality to it.
Assistant: That sounds interesting. I think I might have just the thing. But before I recommend anything, can you tell me what drew you to folk and ambient music in the first place?
User: I think it's because I've always been fascinated by the way music can evoke emotions and create atmospheres. And folk and ambient music seem to do that particularly well.
Assistant: That makes sense. Music can be very powerful in that way. Okay, I think I'm going to take a chance and recommend someone who might fit the bill. But before I do, can you tell me if you've ever heard of Beverly Glenn-Copeland?
User: Actually, yes! I've been listening to his music a lot lately. In fact, I just found out that someone I know is a huge fan of his.
Assistant: No way! That's amazing. What's the story behind that? How did you find out that this person is a fan of Beverly Glenn-Copeland?
User: Well, I was talking to them the other day and they mentioned that they've been listening to his music for years. They said that his album "Keyboard Fantasies" is one of their all-time favorites.
Assistant: Wow, that's great! "Keyboard Fantasies" is definitely a classic. It's amazing how music can bring people together like that. Did this person say what it is about Beverly Glenn-Copeland's music that they love so much?
User: Yeah, they said that it's the way he combines folk and electronic elements to create this unique sound. They also love the way his music can be both calming and thought-provoking at the same time.
Assistant: That's beautiful. I think that's one of the things that makes Beverly Glenn-Copeland's music so special. It's able to evoke a wide range of emotions and moods. Do you think you'll be exploring more of his music now that you know this person is a fan?
User: Hi, I'm feeling a bit stressed lately. I don't know what's wrong with me.
Assistant: Sorry to hear that. It's normal to feel stressed from time to time. Can you tell me a bit more about what's been going on? Has anything changed recently?
User: Not really. I just feel like I'm constantly connected and can't seem to catch a break.
Assistant: That sounds like it could be exhausting. Are you feeling overwhelmed by something specific, or is it more of a general feeling?
User: Hmm, I'm not sure. I just feel like I'm always "on" and can't turn off.
Assistant: I think I understand what you mean. It sounds like you might be feeling a bit burnt out. Have you considered taking some time for yourself to relax and recharge?
User: Yeah, I've tried that. But even when I'm trying to relax, I feel like I'm still connected to... everything.
Assistant: I see. It sounds like technology might be playing a role in how you're feeling. Do you think that's possible?
User: Yeah, I think you might be right. I mean, I'm always checking my phone and scrolling through social media...
Assistant: That can be a big source of stress and anxiety. Have you considered taking a break from social media or limiting your screen time?
User: Actually, that's something I've been thinking about a lot lately. I feel like I've been feeling overwhelmed by the demands of social media and I've decided to take a break from online platforms.
Assistant: That's a great idea! Taking a break from social media can be really beneficial for your mental health. What made you decide to take the plunge and take a break?
User: I just feel like I need to step away from the constant stream of information and comparisons. I want to focus on myself and my own life, rather than comparing it to others.

Assistant: That sounds like a great plan. Remember that it's okay to take a break and prioritize your own needs. You don't have to be constantly connected to be happy and fulfilled.

c101-m1.summary: The Story Stylist is a marketing consulting company based in Beverly.
c101-m1.source_conv_dialogue:
User: The Story Stylist has won the 2018 MarCom Gold Award, its second award for the company’s recently redesigned website.
One of the oldest, largest and most prestigious creative competitions in the world, the MarCom Awards recognizes outstanding achievement by creative professionals involved in the concept, direction, design and production of marketing and communication materials and programs. Judges are industry professionals who look for companies and individuals whose talent exceeds a high standard of excellence and whose work serves as a benchmark for the industry. This year’s submissions included more than 6,000 entries in 300 categories submitted from throughout the world.

User: How can one make reservations for the dinner-and-a-movie lineup at Four Seasons Hotel Los Angeles at Beverly Hills?
Generate according to: ​From February 15 –23, Four Seasons Hotel Los Angeles at Beverly Hills will feature a luxurious dinner-and-a-movie lineup. The hotel will be offering an intimate showing of Oscar nominated films inside the property’s private screening room, followed by a prix-fixe, three-course dinner at Culina. The cinematic package is open to the public, and reservations can be made by calling 310-860-4000.
Dinner starts at 6:30 p.m., followed by the screening at 8 p.m. There will also be a [discounted] matinee on February 18 with a lunch seating at 1:00pm at Culina, followed by a screening of La La Land at 2:15 pm.
All proceeds will benefit the Make a Film Foundation, which grants film wishes to children with serious or life-threatening medical conditions, helping them to create short film legacies by teaming them with noted actors, directors and writers. They believe the art of filmmaking is not only healing and therapeutic, but also offers hope and builds self-esteem.
Celebrated culinary MC and fundraising auctioneer Billy Harris has announced his new dinner series, Hanging with Harris, a lineup of eight intimate, multi-course dining events taking place throughout Los Angeles from February – May. Each Monday night dinner will begin with a cocktail reception hosted by a mixologist from the leading Scotch whisky distiller, William Grant & Sons, followed by a four-course seated dinner with wine pairings from each distinguished chef and a charity auction.
A portion of ticket sales and all proceeds from the auction items will benefit four charities that are close to Harris’ heart: James Beard Foundation, Alex’s Lemonade Stand, No Kid Hungry, and PIGGY BANK.
Union Chef/Owner and James Beard nominee Bruce Kalman has appeared on the Food Network to earn a “Chopped” championship title as well as on Esquire Network to win “Knife Fight.” His Northern Italian cooking style embraces the diverse and abundant produce of California to create exquisitely balanced flavor profiles.
James Beard Foundation “Outstanding Chef,” Suzanne Goin opened Lucques in West Hollywood with her business partner Caroline Styne. The restaurant met with instant success and Suzanne was soon named one of Food and Wine magazine’s “Best New Chefs.” Lucques received praise from Condé Nast Traveler, Gourmet, Bon Appétit and Saveur, including a prestigious 3 star review by the Los Angeles Times.
In addition to “Pastry Chef of the Year,” “Who’s Who of Cooking,” and “Outstanding Restaurant” for Campanile by the James Beard Foundation, Nancy Silverton also received the highest honor given by the James Beard Foundation for “Outstanding Chef” as well as listed as one of the “Most Innovative Women in Food and Drink” by Fortune and Food & Wine.
Michelin-starred Chef Michael Cimarusti combines his knowledge and appreciation of the dynamic nature of seafood with an advocacy for sustainable fishing practices evident in every dish. Located in the heart of West Hollywood, Connie and Ted’s pays homage to Cimarusti’s grandparents and the simple, honest seafood cookery of New England.
David Lentz, husband to Suzanne Goin, is the chef and owner of The Hungry Cat, known for seasonally inspired menus that feature impeccable seafood, bi-coastal American classics, and top-notch cocktails made with farmers’ market ingredients.
Wineries across California gathered in Downtown Santa Barbara on Saturday for a festive showing of high-end libations at the 6th annual Winter Wine Classic. Held outside the Fess Parker Hotel, a luxury resort just steps from the beach, the Winter Wine Classic brought together a solid lineup of purveyors for a mid-sized crowd of joyful guests. Drink, food and fun certainly highlighted the event, with several labels and restaurants to revisit again.
A slew of 90+ point wines made their way to the event, as did bottles that retailed for more than $100. Some highlights included Pegasus Estate Cabernet Sauvignon [Santa Ynez, CA], Rombauer Vineyards Merlot [Napa Valley, CA], J. Lohr Vineyards Chardonnay [Paso Robles, CA], and Nielson Wines Pinot Noir [Santa Barbara, CA] among others.
On the culinary end, Enterprise Fish Co. Led the way with a stunning lobster bisque that was perfect for the winter weather. Patxi’s Pizza Santa Barbara served up some excellent Chicago deep dish, and showed some fun resourcefulness when they placed a delivery order in the middle of the event to replenish their inventory.
Live music kept the upbeat vibe going. And while the event did take place under a tent, the weather did hold out and temperatures stayed quite comfortable.

User: How can one make reservations for the dinner-and-a-movie lineup at Four Seasons Hotel Los Angeles at Beverly Hills?
Generate according to: ​From February 15 –23, Four Seasons Hotel Los Angeles at Beverly Hills will feature a luxurious dinner-and-a-movie lineup. The hotel will be offering an intimate showing of Oscar nominated films inside the property’s private screening room, followed by a prix-fixe, three-course dinner at Culina. The cinematic package is open to the public, and reservations can be made by calling 310-860-4000.
Dinner starts at 6:30 p.m., followed by the screening at 8 p.m. There will also be a [discounted] matinee on February 18 with a lunch seating at 1:00pm at Culina, followed by a screening of La La Land at 2:15 pm.
All proceeds will benefit the Make a Film Foundation, which grants film wishes to children with serious or life-threatening medical conditions, helping them to create short film legacies by teaming them with noted actors, directors and writers. Celebrated culinary MC and fundraising auctioneer Billy Harris has announced his new dinner series, Hanging with Harris, a lineup of eight intimate, multi-course dining events taking place throughout Los Angeles from February – May. Each Monday night dinner will begin with a cocktail reception hosted by a mixologist from the leading Scotch whisky distiller, William Grant & Sons, followed by a four-course seated dinner with wine pairings from each distinguished chef and a charity auction.
A portion of ticket sales and all proceeds from the auction items will benefit four charities that are close to Harris’ heart: James Beard Foundation, Alex’s Lemonade Stand, No Kid Hungry, and PIGGY BANK.
Union Chef/Owner and James Beard nominee Bruce Kalman has appeared on the Food Network to earn a “Chopped” championship title as well as on Esquire Network to win “Knife Fight.” His Northern Italian cooking style embraces the diverse and abundant produce of California to create exquisitely balanced flavor profiles.
James Beard Foundation “Outstanding Chef,” Suzanne Goin opened Lucques in West Hollywood with her business partner Caroline Styne. The restaurant met with instant success and Suzanne was soon named one of Food and Wine magazine’s “Best New Chefs.” Lucques received praise from Condé Nast Traveler, Gourmet, Bon Appétit and Saveur, including a prestigious 3 star review by the Los Angeles Times.
In addition to “Pastry Chef of the Year,” “Who’s Who of Cooking,” and “Outstanding Restaurant” for Campanile by the James Beard Foundation, Nancy Silverton also received the highest honor given by the James Beard Foundation for “Outstanding Chef” as well as listed as one of the “Most Innovative Women in Food and Drink” by Fortune and Food & Wine.
Michelin-starred Chef Michael Cimarusti combines his knowledge and appreciation of the dynamic nature of seafood with an advocacy for sustainable fishing practices evident in every dish. Located in the heart of West Hollywood, Connie and Ted’s pays homage to Cimarusti’s grandparents and the simple, honest seafood cookery of New England.
David Lentz, husband to Suzanne Goin, is the chef and owner of The Hungry Cat, known for seasonally inspired menus that feature impeccable seafood, bi-coastal American classics, and top-notch cocktails made with farmers’ market ingredients.
Wineries across California gathered in Downtown Santa Barbara on Saturday for a festive showing of high-end libations at the 6th annual Winter Wine Classic. Held outside the Fess Parker Hotel, a luxury resort just steps from the beach, the Winter Wine Classic brought together a solid lineup of purveyors for a mid-sized crowd of joyful guests. Drink, food and fun certainly highlighted the event, with several labels and restaurants to revisit again.
A slew of 90+ point wines made their way to the event, as did bottles that retailed for more than $100. Some highlights included Pegasus Estate Cabernet Sauvignon [Santa Ynez, CA], Rombauer Vineyards Merlot [Napa Valley, CA], J. Lohr Vineyards Chardonnay [Paso Robles, CA], and Nielson Wines Pinot Noir [Santa Barbara, CA] among others.
On the culinary end, Enterprise Fish Co. Led the way with a stunning lobster bisque that was perfect for the winter weather. Patxi’s Pizza Santa Barbara served up some excellent Chicago deep dish, and showed some fun resourcefulness when they placed a delivery order in the middle of the event to replenish their inventory.
Live music kept the upbeat vibe going. And while the event did take place under a tent, the weather did hold out and temperatures stayed quite comfortable.

A portion of ticket sales and all proceeds from the auction items will benefit four charities that are close to Harris’ heart: James Beard Foundation, Alex’s Lemonade Stand, No Kid Hungry, and PIGGY BANK.
Union Chef/Owner and James Beard nominee Bruce Kalman has appeared on the Food Network to earn a “Chopped” championship title as well as on Esquire Network to win “Knife Fight.” His Northern Italian cooking style embraces the diverse and abundant produce of California to create exquisitely balanced flavor profiles.
James Beard Foundation “Outstanding Chef,” Suzanne Goin opened Lucques in West Hollywood with her business partner Caroline Styne. In addition to “Pastry Chef of the Year,” “Who’s Who of Cooking,” and “Outstanding Restaurant” for Campanile by the James Beard Foundation, Nancy Silverton also received the highest honor given by the James Beard Foundation for “Outstanding Chef” as well as listed as one of the “Most Innovative Women in Food and Drink” by Fortune and Food & Wine.
Michelin-starred Chef Michael Cimarusti combines his knowledge and appreciation of the dynamic nature of seafood with an advocacy for sustainable fishing practices evident in every dish. Located in the heart of West Hollywood, Connie and Ted’s pays homage to Cimarusti’s grandparents and the simple, honest seafood cookery of New England.
David Lentz, husband to Suzanne Goin, is the chef and owner of The Hungry Cat, known for seasonally inspired menus that feature impeccable seafood, bi-coastal American classics, and top-notch cocktails made with farmers’ market ingredients.
Wineries across California gathered in Downtown Santa Barbara on Saturday for a festive showing of high-end libations at the 6th annual Winter Wine Classic. Held outside the Fess Parker Hotel, a luxury resort just steps from the beach, the Winter Wine Classic brought together a solid lineup of purveyors for a mid-sized crowd of joyful guests. Drink, food and fun certainly highlighted the event, with several labels and restaurants to revisit again.
A slew of 90+ point wines made their way to the event, as did bottles that retailed for more than $100. Some highlights included Pegasus Estate Cabernet Sauvignon [Santa Ynez, CA], Rombauer Vineyards Merlot [Napa Valley, CA], J. Lohr Vineyards Chardonnay [Paso Robles, CA], and Nielson Wines Pinot Noir [Santa Barbara, CA] among others.
On the culinary end, Enterprise Fish Co. Led the way with a stunning lobster bisque that was perfect for the winter weather. Patxi’s Pizza Santa Barbara served up some excellent Chicago deep dish, and showed some fun resourcefulness when they placed a delivery order in the middle of the event to replenish their inventory.
Live music kept the upbeat vibe going. And while the event did take place under a tent, the weather did hold out and temperatures stayed quite comfortable.
